questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Taiwan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Taiwan article.

questions.proof: Its de facto capital is Taipei.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Taiwan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Taiwan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Taiwan article.

questions.proof: Taiwan is located southeast of the Chinese mainland, south of Japan, and north of the Philippines.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Taiwan's government, "does not want China's 'one country, two systems' ", according to media (in _____).”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Taiwan article.

questions.proof: Taiwan's government, "does not want China's 'one country, two systems' ", according to media (in 2025).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Republic of China once governed all of China (from _____ to 1949) but moved to the island of Taiwan after their defeat in a Chinese civil war.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Taiwan article, under the heading “Status of Taiwan”.

questions.proof: The ROC government governed most of China mainland from 1911 to 1949, before losing control of China mainland to the PRC.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Communist Party of China (CCP) establishes _____ as the capital of The People's Republic of China (PRC).”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “establishes”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Taiwan article, under the heading “Timeline”.

questions.proof: The Communist Party of China (CCP) establishes Beijing as the capital of The People's Republic of China (PRC).
